research_updates.title: Proposed expansion agreement expired
research_updates.notes: Hammond reports that the development agreement for 301 Digital Crossroads expired after its June 30, 2026 deadline. The city says it will offer no further extensions of that agreement. The 2025 proposed expansion and associated payment promises are not treated as active commitments or realized receipts. This update concerns the proposed expansion; it does not establish closure of the existing DX-1 facility.

source.title: Hammond Announces Expiration of Data Center Development Agreement
source.notes: Official city announcement retrieved as HTML. The proposed expansion agreement at 301 Digital Crossroads expired after unmet June 30, 2026 milestones and two extensions. This does not establish closure of the existing Digital Crossroad facility.

research_updates.title: Developer reports more than $80 million spent with local contractors
research_updates.notes: Official Council minutes record Decennial's co-founder describing more than $80 million spent with local contractors on the existing Building 1. The amount is a cumulative, developer-reported lower bound. Local geography, annual timing, contractor payments, worker counts, payroll and multiplier effects remain unverified.

source.title: Hammond Common Council Meeting Minutes — June 9, 2025
source.notes: The official minutes record a statement by Decennial Group co-founder David Pavlik during Council consideration of the later 301 Digital Crossroads proposal. He describes the existing Building 1, acquired mid-construction in 2021, and reports well over $80 million spent with local contractors for electrical, mechanical, plumbing, roofing, re-roofing and fiber work. The amount is developer testimony preserved in a public record, not an audited expenditure schedule. The minutes do not define local geography, spending start date, payroll, worker count, job-years or multiplier effects.

research_updates.title: Owner-funded improvement district separates estimates from City credit
research_updates.notes: Ordinance 9496 estimates Building 1 capital expenditure at $88,656,629 and creates potential owner special assessments for project debt and district expenses. The ordinance does not pledge City or state faith, credit or taxing power, and assigns excess zone expenses to the project owner. The application retains the cost and assessment caps as forecasts because no final EID bond, schedule, collection or expenditure was verified.

source.title: Hammond Ordinance 9496 — DX Hammond Economic Improvement District
source.notes: The enacted ordinance and attached petition establish a 67.52-acre economic improvement district for privately funded project debt. Exhibit J-1 gives an $88,656,629 Building 1 capital-cost estimate. Section 46 caps annual special assessments at $3,415,000 in Zone 1 and $3,415,000 in Zone 2, with Zone 3 exempt; assessments may remain for up to 25 years after an EID bond is issued. The ordinance says City, state and political-subdivision faith, credit and taxing power are not pledged to EID debt, and excess zone expenses are payable by the project owner. No EID bond issuance, final assessment schedule, collections or expenditures were verified in this review. The attached U.S. Chamber typical-data-center multipliers are contextual and are not encoded as Hammond facts.

research_updates.title: State debt register shows the existing TIF bond but no separate EID debt
research_updates.notes: Indiana Gateway's live Hammond Civil City outstanding-debt register includes the Series 2019 Data Center bond and no separately named DX Hammond Economic Improvement District or EID bond. This closes one public-record screen, not the entire financing question: a private obligation, unreported closing or separately administered instrument could fall outside the City register. EID bills, owner payments, district receipts and expenditures remain unverified.

source.title: Indiana Gateway Hammond Civil City Outstanding Bond/Lease Register
source.notes: The live Hammond Civil City outstanding-debt filter lists 33 debt names, including the existing City of Hammond Taxable Economic Development Revenue Bonds, Series 2019 (Data Center). It does not list a DX Hammond Economic Improvement District bond or another EID-labelled obligation. This is a bounded screen of Hammond Civil City's current self-reported debt register; it does not prove that no private obligation, unreported closing or separately administered instrument exists.

research_updates.title: Audited report separates operating scale, private financing and fund accounting
research_updates.notes: Principal reports year-end cost basis, fair value, 115,652 square feet, 15 MW commissioned, 89.3% leased and occupied, and asset-specific equipment line-of-credit balances. Cost basis, fair value and private debt remain separate stocks; neither debt-balance changes nor the report's fund-wide real-estate-improvements roll-forward are treated as Hammond annual capital spending. Utilization is not converted into MW, revenue, employment or measured electricity use.

source.title: Principal Digital Real Estate Fund (A), LP 2025 Annual Report — Audited Financial Statements
source.notes: Audited fund statements repeat the Hammond financing terms and report 2024-2025 project TIF revenues used toward loan repayments. The report states that these revenues were generated solely by real-estate tax payments made by Hammond Data Center. The audited consolidated schedule reports Hammond's 2024 and 2025 cost basis and fair value; the manager update reports 115,652 square feet, 15 MW commissioned and 89.3% leased and occupied at year-end 2025. The debt note reports asset-specific equipment line-of-credit balances. Its separate real-estate-improvements roll-forward covers the entire multi-property Aggregator and is not assigned to Hammond.

research_updates.title: Development agreement adds a job forecast, local-labor requirements and water-permit limits
research_updates.notes: The agreement anticipated approximately 40 full-time jobs and required good-faith priority for Hammond, Lake County and Indiana contractors and workers. Section 1.9(B)(2) also required the developer to retain relevant compliance data and provide it to the Redevelopment Commission at least quarterly until construction completion. The study treats the jobs as a forecast, the labor terms as requirements without realized participation data, and the water figures as permit capacities rather than use.

It also states prospective investment and job figures and water-permit capacities. The agreement does not itself report realized hiring, payroll, measured water use or confirmation that the permit transfer occurred.

research_updates.title: Contemporaneous completion report supplies a 17-employee operating snapshot
research_updates.notes: Data Center Dynamics reported 17 facility employees and separately described an expectation that customer staff could bring on-site employment to roughly 40.
